1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists
60:

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists
60:

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.

7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists

7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.

9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.

14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never

7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists
60:

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists
60:

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists

    let i be 2
    while i * i <= num do

    end

    let num be num + 1
end

end

1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists

7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.

msgs.content:
1: Plink language reference
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: Plink is a small line-based programming language. Each statement is on its own line. Blocks (loops and ifs) are
6: closed with a line containing only `end`. Indentation is ignored but recommended. A Plink program is just a list of
7: statements: there is no main function. Integers and text are the only kinds of value, plus true/false and lists.
8: 
9: ## Comments
10: 
11: A line starting with the word `note` is a comment.
12: 
13:     note this line is ignored
14: 
15: ## Variables
16: 
17: `let` declares a new variable. `set` changes a variable that already exists. Using `set` on a name that was never
18: declared with `let` is an error, and so is declaring the same name twice with `let`.
19: 
20:     let total be 0
21:     let name be "plink"
22:     set total to total + 5
23: 
24: ## Printing
25: 
26: `show` prints one or more values separated by spaces, followed by a newline.
27: 
28:     show total
29:     show "x is", 3
30:     show 1, 2, 3
31: 
32: prints
33: 
34:     5
35:     x is 3
36:     1 2 3
37: 
38: ## Numbers and operators
39: 
40: Arithmetic: `+` `-` `*` and the words `div` (whole-number division, rounding down) and `mod` (remainder).
41: 
42:     show 17 div 5
43:     show 17 mod 5
44: 
45: prints 3 then 2.
46: 
47: Comparison: `=` (equal), `<>` (not equal), `<` `>` `<=` `>=`. Logic: `and`, `or`, `not`. Values `true` and `false`.
48: Parentheses group as usual. Note: `==`, `!=`, `%`, `//` and `**` are not Plink operators.
49: 
50: ## Text
51: 
52: Text is written in double quotes. `&` joins two pieces of text. `text(n)` turns a number into text.
53: 
54:     let s be "ab" & "cd"
55:     show s & text(42)
56: 
57: prints `abcd42`.
58: 
59: ## Lists
